# IPQmedia Field Guide

> Marketing and lead generation resources for architecture firms, written by IPQmedia, a client acquisition agency for US architecture firms. Every guide covers both residential firms (clients are homeowners) and commercial firms (clients are developers and business owners), with real data and verified sources.

IPQmedia runs done-for-you paid advertising (primarily Meta) that gets architecture firms qualified client leads on a pay-per-performance basis. Founder: Arseniy Volosevich. Program details: https://beam.ipqmedia.com/program

Canonical URL form for every page below is without a trailing slash. Index of all guides: https://ipqmedia.com/resources

## Core guides

- [Architecture marketing](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/architecture-marketing): The complete system: get found, convert, earn trust, follow up. The hub every guide below links into.
- [Lead generation for architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/lead-generation-for-architects): How architecture firms get qualified client inquiries on purpose instead of waiting on referrals.
- [Meta ads for architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/meta-ads-for-architects): Why Facebook and Instagram ads are the demand engine for both residential and commercial firms.
- [Marketing for residential architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/marketing-for-residential-architects): Reaching homeowners planning a build or major renovation.
- [Marketing for commercial architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/marketing-for-commercial-architects): Reaching developers, business owners and facilities directors.

## Channel guides

- [SEO for architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/seo-for-architects): Organic search as the compounding layer.
- [Google Ads for architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/google-ads-for-architects): Search ads, real CPC data, where they fit.
- [Google Business Profile for architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/google-business-profile-for-architects): The map pack as a free capture layer.
- [Content marketing for architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/content-marketing-for-architects): What to publish and the buyer questions worth answering.
- [Email marketing for architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/email-marketing-for-architects): Follow-up and nurture, where most inquiries are lost.
- [LinkedIn for architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/linkedin-for-architects): A real channel for commercial firms, a staff room for residential ones.
- [Social media for architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/social-media-for-architects): What posting actually produces. Across 24.4 million Instagram posts, single-image reach fell 21.96% in a year while brands published 24.04% more. Across 18 IPQmedia-run architecture firm ad accounts, a median account needs roughly 825 impressions per lead at a median $58.45 cost per lead.
- [Houzz for architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/houzz-for-architects): Whether Houzz advertising is worth it for an architecture firm. Houzz does not publish its ad pricing; Capterra lists Houzz Pro from $399 a month. Houzz's own 2026 study of 20,000+ users found 27% of renovating homeowners planning to spend under $10,000 and 17% over $100,000.
- [RFPs for architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/rfp-for-architects): Where architecture RFPs get posted, why public agencies must select on qualifications rather than fee, and the Deltek 2026 median capture rate of 44.4% across 896 firms, the lowest since 2019.
- [Referral systems for architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/referral-systems-for-architects): Turning word of mouth from luck into a system.
- [Partnerships for architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/partnerships-for-architects): Standing arrangements with realtors, builders, developers and design-builders.
- [Direct mail for architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/direct-mail-for-architects): A warm-list follow-up layer, not a discovery engine.
- [PR and press for architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/pr-and-press-for-architects): Press and awards as a credibility layer.
- [Website design for architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/website-design-for-architects): Fixing the portfolio that doesn't convert.
- [Video marketing for architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/video-marketing-for-architects): Film as ad creative first, owned library second.
- [Branding for architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/branding-for-architects): What a brand fixes, what it cannot, and what it costs.

## Comparisons

- [Meta ads vs Google Ads for architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/meta-ads-vs-google-ads-for-architects): Creating demand against capturing it, with real click costs for both.
- [Pay per lead vs retainer for architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/pay-per-lead-vs-retainer-for-architects): The three ways firms pay for marketing, and who carries the risk in each.

## Original data and benchmarks

- [Architecture marketing benchmark report 2026](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/architecture-marketing-benchmark-report-2026): Per-firm quartiles from 16 US architecture firm ad accounts. Median cost per lead $57, full range $13 to $100. Includes findings published nowhere else for this profession: cost per lead drifts up with account age, and 56% of ads produce zero leads.
- [Architecture marketing statistics and costs 2026](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/architecture-marketing-statistics-and-costs-2026): Market costs roundup. IPQmedia's own blended $55 cost per lead and $0.95 cost per click across $95,539 of spend, next to AIA/Deltek billings data, Deltek Clarity win rates, PSMJ marketing spend shares and current search click costs.
- [Architecture client demand by metro 2026](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/architecture-client-demand-by-metro-2026): Google search volume and click cost for architect intent across 16 US metros, next to the adjacent trades clients hire instead. Architect intent 13,040 searches a month against 68,990 for those trades.

## Firm types

- [Marketing for landscape architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/marketing-for-landscape-architects): Buyers search "landscape designer near me" 14,800 times a month against 4,400 for "landscape architect near me", plus the full 12-month demand curve and its November collapse.
- [Marketing for high-end residential architects](https://ipqmedia.com/resources/marketing-for-high-end-residential-architects): Firms that name an affluence target pay a median $71.52 per lead against $31.02, and the mechanism is click-to-lead conversion, not expensive reach.
